numerical_failure.observed_behavior: compress_matrix treated an inequality row as redundant when it was any scalar multiple (including negative) of a kept row with matching right-hand side ratio, so negative-multiple rows were dropped and the feasible set was enlarged; e.g. min z s.t. z <= 1, z >= 1 plus duplicated equalities was reported unbounded instead of optimal at 1. Separately, when CVXOPT presolve merged duplicate inequality rows, duals of original constraints were recovered as P_leq @ z, giving each merged row a scaled copy of the full compressed multiplier; duplicated constraints received duals summing to (1 + ratio^2) times the correct value (e.g. z >= 1 stated twice produced duals 1.0 and 1.0 where the sum must be 1.0).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Only positive-ratio rows should be merged (negative multiples kept), so the problem solves to optimal value 1. Recovered duals should satisfy stationarity, G_orig.T @ y_orig == G_compr.T @ z, with each compressed dual assigned entirely to the kept row and zero to dropped duplicates, so the duals of duplicated constraints sum to the correct value (1.0 in the z >= 1 example).

Fix uses an expansion matrix assigning each compressed dual entirely to the kept row and zero to dropped duplicates, so G_orig.T @ y_orig == G_compr.T @ z.
